subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The reduction division that halves the chromosome number occurs at which point in meiosis?
options: meiosis I, when homologous chromosomes separate
questions.explain: Meiosis I is the reduction division: homologous chromosomes are separated, halving the chromosome number from diploid to haploid.

questions.q: Red-green colour blindness is X-linked recessive. A carrier mother and an unaffected father have children. What proportion of their sons are expected to be colour blind?
questions.explain: Sons inherit one of the mother's two X chromosomes, so half receive the affected X and are colour blind.

questions.q: In incomplete dominance, a cross between a red (RR) and white (rr) flower gives pink offspring. The F2 phenotypic ratio from crossing two pink plants is:
questions.explain: With incomplete dominance the heterozygote is pink, so the F2 shows a 1:2:1 genotype-matched phenotype ratio.

questions.q: Two genes A and B are autosomally linked. A parent of genotype AaBb (with A and B on one chromosome, a and b on the other) is test-crossed. The most common offspring will be:
options: The two parental combinations (AB and ab)
Equal numbers of all four genotypes
questions.explain: Linkage means parental allele combinations predominate, with recombinants being the minority.

questions.q: A substitution mutation in a coding region may have no effect on the polypeptide produced. This is most likely because:
options: The degenerate nature of the code means the new codon may still code for the same amino acid
The mutation occurs in an intron only
questions.explain: Owing to degeneracy, an altered codon can still specify the same amino acid (a synonymous/silent mutation).

questions.q: A high value of an index of diversity (e.g. Simpson's index) for a habitat indicates:
options: Many species each fairly evenly represented
Few species and many individuals of one species
questions.explain: A high diversity index reflects many species in relatively even proportions, indicating a more stable ecosystem.

questions.q: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are reproductively isolated by:
options: A behavioural difference within the same area
A change in mating season only
A geographical barrier such as a mountain or river
questions.explain: In allopatric speciation a physical/geographical barrier separates populations, allowing them to diverge.

questions.q: A cell with a diploid number of 8 (2n=8) undergoing meiosis will produce gametes containing how many chromosomes, and how many distinct combinations are possible from independent assortment alone?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid (n=4), and with 4 homologous pairs independent assortment gives 2 to the power 4 = 16 possible chromosome combinations.

questions.q: Ribosomes found free in the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell are:
options: made of pure protein with no RNA
bound only to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
70S, the same as in the mitochondrion's matrix
80S, larger than the 70S ribosomes of prokaryotes
questions.explain: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, whereas prokaryotic and organellar ribosomes are the smaller 70S type.

questions.q: The function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is to:
options: synthesise proteins via attached ribosomes and transport them
questions.explain: The RER is studded with ribosomes that synthesise proteins, which are folded and transported through its cisternae.

questions.q: In PCR, the function of the primers is to:
options: Provide a starting point with a free 3'-OH for DNA polymerase
Cut the DNA at specific sites
questions.explain: Primers anneal to the template and provide the free 3' end that DNA polymerase needs to begin synthesis.

questions.q: Hybrid sterility, such as the infertile mule from a horse and donkey, is an example of a:
questions.explain: The hybrid forms but is sterile, so isolation acts after the zygote forms, making it postzygotic.

questions.q: Disruptive selection differs from the other types because it:
options: Favours both extreme phenotypes at the expense of intermediates
questions.explain: Disruptive selection favours both extremes and selects against intermediate phenotypes, potentially leading to two distinct groups.

questions.q: The resolution of an electron microscope is greater than that of a light microscope because:
options: electrons travel more slowly than light
electrons have a longer wavelength than light
electrons have a much shorter wavelength than visible light
the specimen is stained more heavily
questions.explain: Resolution depends on wavelength; the very short wavelength of an electron beam allows much finer detail to be distinguished.

questions.q: What is the function of tRNA during translation?
options: To bring specific amino acids to the ribosome according to its anticodon
To unwind the DNA double helix
To carry the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome
questions.explain: Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and pairs its anticodon with the complementary mRNA codon.

questions.q: In the biological species concept, two organisms belong to the same species if they can:
questions.explain: The biological species concept defines a species as a group able to interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

questions.q: Decreased acetylation of histones (deacetylation) tends to:
options: Make chromatin more condensed and decrease transcription
questions.explain: Histone deacetylation increases positive charge, tightening DNA-histone binding and condensing chromatin to reduce transcription.

questions.q: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.explain: In anaphase the centromeres divide and spindle fibres pull the sister chromatids to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.q: The founder effect occurs when:
options: A large population is split equally by a barrier
A small group establishes a new population carrying only a subset of the original gene pool
questions.explain: A few founding individuals carry only part of the parent population's genetic variation, skewing allele frequencies in the new population.

questions.q: Haemophilia is more common in males than females because:
options: The allele is carried on the Y chromosome
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed
questions.explain: The recessive allele is X-linked, and males (XY) express it with only one copy as they have no second X to mask it.

questions.q: Continuous variation produces a frequency distribution that is typically:
questions.explain: Polygenic continuous traits give a normal distribution with most individuals near the mean.

questions.q: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) differs from a scanning electron microscope (SEM) in that the TEM:
options: has lower resolution than the SEM
passes electrons through a thin specimen to give a high-resolution 2D image of internal structure
can be used on living specimens
questions.explain: A TEM transmits electrons through an ultra-thin section, producing a detailed 2D image of internal ultrastructure, whereas an SEM gives a 3D surface view.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the cell cycle?
questions.explain: Interphase comprises G1 (growth), S (DNA replication) and G2 (preparation), followed by mitosis and cytokinesis.

questions.q: Restriction endonucleases that leave 'sticky ends' are useful in recombinant DNA technology because:
options: The single-stranded overhangs allow complementary fragments to anneal before ligation
They cut DNA into blunt fragments only
They permanently join DNA without ligase
questions.explain: Sticky ends are short single-stranded overhangs that base-pair with complementary ends, allowing DNA ligase to join the fragments.

questions.q: In semi-conservative replication, each new DNA molecule consists of:
options: Fragments of both original strands recombined
One original strand and one new strand
questions.explain: Each daughter molecule conserves one parental strand which acts as a template for one newly synthesised strand.

questions.q: In a cross of two heterozygous black guinea pigs (Bb x Bb) where black is dominant to white, the probability that a single offspring is white is:
questions.explain: Bb x Bb gives a 3:1 ratio, so each offspring has a 1 in 4 chance of being homozygous recessive (white).

questions.q: The magnification and resolution of a microscope are different properties; resolution is best defined as:
options: the minimum distance between two points at which they can still be distinguished as separate
how many times larger the image appears than the object
the depth of field of the lens
questions.explain: Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate; it is limited by the wavelength of radiation used, not by magnification.

questions.q: Why does a heterozygous female carrier of an X-linked recessive condition usually not show the condition?
options: The allele is on the Y chromosome
X-linked alleles are never expressed in females
She has no copies of the allele
Her second X chromosome carries a dominant normal allele that masks it
questions.explain: Her normal dominant allele on the other X chromosome masks the recessive allele, so she is an unaffected carrier.

questions.q: Meiosis generates genetic variation partly through independent assortment, which occurs because:
options: maternal and paternal chromosomes orient randomly at the metaphase plate, so combinations in gametes vary
homologous chromosomes exchange alleles by crossing over
questions.explain: The random orientation of homologous pairs in metaphase I means each gamete receives a different mix of maternal and paternal chromosomes.

questions.q: In sex linkage, a characteristic feature of pedigrees for X-linked recessive traits is that:
options: An affected father passes the allele to all his daughters but none of his sons
Affected fathers always pass it to their sons
questions.explain: A father passes his single X to all daughters (making them carriers) but passes his Y, not his X, to sons.
